I'm thinking through ENG-2348's testing requirements: since the style guide explicitly mandates unit tests for new functionality, this component needs a render test covering both flag states—showing the callout with title when disabled, rendering nothing when enabled—to properly encode the Done When criteria.

Beyond closing that finding, I need to fold in a re-review of the round-1 changes covering the delta between commits.

Switching to ENG-2195's review, I'm hitting a fork point on Done When 2's format validation requirement—only the invalid character portion is actually verified, so I need to work through two possible interpretations of that boundary.

Narrow reading only needs the character rule satisfied and can cite ENG-2346's placeholder precedent while flagging the uniqueness implication. The broader reading pulls in full validateNodeFormat with fallback logic, canonicalization of capitalized content tags, and a new default-collision rule, but that risks overlapping scope with ENG-2346 and the documented Out of Scope boundary—so this needs a call from sid or mdroidian, and I should form a recommendation on which way to go by checking what validateNodeFormat actually requires for a case like `{Content}`.

Tracing through the collision logic, two Roam node types only collide into a new Obsidian type if their names differ but their rendered formats match after normalization—if the names match (like "Claim" to "Claim" or "Question" to "Question"), findLocalNodeTypeMatch just returns the existing local type and no new type gets created.

But the real problem is P2-1: once this collision happens, validateNodeType checks format uniqueness across all node types including the imported one, so the user becomes permanently unable to save any edits to their own local type—every field save triggers the validator and fails. That's a genuine regression this PR introduces, since bracketed formats never used to collide with valid local formats before. I'm weighing fixes: fall back to a name-derived default format on collision, append a disambiguating suffix, or skip normalization entirely when it would produce a collision.

Given that "passes existing format validation" implies uniqueness, I think the correct interpretation is Fork B — validate the normalized format against the vault's existing node types, and if it collides, reject or adjust it rather than silently creating an ambiguous duplicate, since duplicate formats would also break title-to-type matching elsewhere in the system.

I'm weighing a minimal fallback approach: normalize, then try the name-derived default if validation fails, though it's unclear what to do if even that collides. I'm also considering whether canonicalizing `{Content}` to `{content}` fits the spirit of normalizing incoming formats, and thinking through why format collisions between node types are genuinely problematic since files become indistinguishable by title.

I want to avoid inventing numeric suffixes or auto-merging types across schemas, since that's explicitly a non-goal. I'm leaning toward proposing a concrete default to sid: canonicalize the content placeholder, fall back to the name-derived format on failure, and only as a last resort append the smallest numeric suffix if even that collides.

That matches what the reviewer called Fork B: validate normalized format first, fall back to the name-derived default on collision, and if that also collides, just accept it as a rare documented residual rather than inventing a new suffix rule.

On scope, I'm checking whether Fork B counts as the out-of-scope "broader node format validation" — but since it's only applying existing validation at import time rather than expanding validation logic, it stays in scope and aligns with what ENG-2346 is asking for regarding unsupported placeholders in Obsidian node titles.

Now I need to check whether ENG-2346 and ENG-2323 both state missing `{content}` "remains invalid" — if so, Fork B's fallback behavior for missing `{content}` would directly conflict with that documented decision, so I should pull up both tickets to verify before framing a question for sid about which approach to take.

I think I'll batch the fork question for sid at a natural checkpoint rather than block on it now, and meanwhile hand the ENG-2195 implementer the non-fork fixes (P2-2, P3-1 through P3-3, the PR body, and the Linear reply draft) to keep things moving while the fork decision is pending. Looking at P2-2 more closely, the stated reasoning seems factually wrong since exported specs can include imported types with bracketed formats, and both the create and merge paths in specImport.ts store these un-normalized.

Actually I'm realizing the repo's own vocabulary matters here — recent commits like "Add conflict resolution step to the Obsidian schema import modal" and "Add schema import file picker" show that "schema import" specifically refers to the specImport.ts flow in this codebase, which reframes how I should interpret the ticket's scope.

Looking at specImport's two write locations, normalizing each would take about two lines calling normalizeImportedNodeFormat. But I'm wary of the merge path through mergeNodeTypeFields, since normalizing format there would override what the user explicitly chose during merge, and could make an otherwise valid local type invalid if the merge was intentional.

This is a second fork point — the fix is cheap (two call sites plus tests), but it's unclear whether to include it. Including it closes a real round-trip gap for exported imported types, but legacy vaults already fall outside scope per the ticket, so this gap mostly affects a narrow, rare case of legacy-imported types exported via spec files. I'm torn between deferring this to a follow-up ticket or folding it in now.

Checking the project's non-goals confirms Fork B's fallback is format adjustment, not cross-schema translation, so it stays in scope. I'm framing D1 for sid as a choice between Fork A (character rule only, with uniqueness caveat documented) versus Fork B (full validateNodeFormat with name-derived fallback), leaning toward recommending Fork B since a collision would otherwise block a user from saving their own local type — though I want to double-check that harm is actually real before committing to that recommendation.

Tracing through NodeTypeSettings validation, I confirm that if a user's local "Claim" type and an imported "Claims" type normalize to the same format string, editing the local type fails uniqueness validation — a genuine regression under Fork A that Fork B's fallback would avoid, since name matches mean no import happens in the first place, and collisions mainly surface when names differ.

Canonicalizing formats like `{Content}` seems safe since decorate/extract are case-insensitive, and I need to check ENG-2346 to see whether the missing-`{content}` case still applies during import, plus revisit whether specImport.ts's two call sites should include or defer this logic.

Two results came in: for #1506 (ENG-2348), I'll just have the implementer add a short render test using the existing jsdom component tests as a template. For #1507 (ENG-2195), there's a real disagreement about what Done When 2 requires, so before raising it with you I'm reviewing ENG-2346 and ENG-2323, which already handle placeholder behavior.

* Obsidian node titles support only `{content}`, but the Format field can accept additional placeholders without warning.
* A format such as `EVD - {content} - {Source}` contains an unsupported placeholder. Schema import can also copy these formats from Roam.

## Solution

* During manual node type creation or editing, show an inline warning under the Format field for placeholders other than `{content}`. Use the existing double-bracket validation message as the UI pattern.
* [ENG-2346](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2346/ignore-unsupported-placeholders-when-constructing-obsidian-node-titles>) covers title construction for the same formats during local node creation and import. This ticket covers only the UI warning.

## Done When

* The Format field identifies unsupported placeholders and explains that only `{content}` is supported. The warning appears during manual node type creation or editing.
* Verification covers `{Source}`, an arbitrary unsupported placeholder, and multiple unsupported placeholders. Content-only formats do not show an unsupported-placeholder warning. Missing `{content}` remains invalid.
* Import does not add placeholder warnings or notices.

## Out of Scope

* Changing title construction, ignored-placeholder behavior, or import behavior. Those changes are covered by [ENG-2346](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2346/ignore-unsupported-placeholders-when-constructing-obsidian-node-titles>).

{"id":"ENG-2346","uuid":"a9972593-2a3e-438c-8689-a65eacc24912","title":"Ignore unsupported placeholders when constructing Obsidian node titles on import","description":">>> ## Problem

* Obsidian node titles support `{content}`, but settings can accept additional placeholders and schema import can copy them from Roam. A format such as `EVD - {content} - {Source}` then makes import fall back to the original title.
* Source information already has a separate relation path through [ENG-2140](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2140>).

>>>

>>> ## Solution

ENG-2348 (#1506) is getting a short render test. Everything else keeps running, but ENG-2195 (#1507) needs two decisions from you.

**ENG-2195 Done When 2 says "the result passes the existing format validation".** The PR only satisfies the invalid-character part of it. Running the real code showed two gaps:
- `[[CLM]] - {Content}` becomes `CLM - {Content}`, which fails Obsidian's case-sensitive `{content}` rule.
- `[[HYP]] - {content}` becomes `HYP - {content}`. If a local type with a different name already uses that format, the two collide.

The collision is new harm from this PR. Obsidian checks uniqueness on every settings save (`NodeTypeSettings.tsx:770`), so it would refuse to save any edit to the user's own local type. The imported type is read-only, so the user can't fix it from that side. Roam's `[[CLM]]` and `[[QUE]]` defaults normalize to exactly Obsidian's defaults, so this happens whenever the type names differ.

- **Option B (my recommendation):** at import, if the normalized format still fails `validateNodeFormat` against the vault's types, fall back to the name-derived default (normalized). Canonicalize `{Content}` to `{content}` first. If the default also collides, store it anyway and document that. This is about 20–30 lines in a small pure helper with tests.
- **Option A:** keep the character rule only. The PR body documents the collision and cites ENG-2346 for the `{content}` rule.

**`specImport.ts` (importing schema files) also stores formats without normalizing them.** It's only exposed through types imported before this PR, which the ticket puts out of scope for rewriting.
- **Recommended:** defer it with a follow-up ticket, and fix the PR body's wrong reason for skipping it.
- **Alternative:** include it now, about 4 lines.

Whichever you pick, the implementer also gets the reviewer's other fixes: normalize the name-derived default, reword a comment, fix one test title, and update the PR body.

**One outward action needs your OK.** Michael's "possible duplication" comment on ENG-2195 is unanswered. I have a reply drafted:

> Not a duplicate of ENG-2176. ENG-2176 escapes regex metacharacters when a format becomes a match expression. ENG-2195 removes `#`, `^`, `[`, `]` and `|` from imported formats before they're stored. They overlap only on `^` and `|`, and escaping alone doesn't fix `|`: `sanitizeFileName` drops it from file names, so an escaped `\|` still doesn't match. The two branches don't touch the same files.

Should I post it on ENG-2195 as you? I've left the same question on ENG-2176 alone.

content.thinking:
This confirms N1: the field rename from `template` to `template_content` happened in ENG-2202, so legacy Roam rows synced before that merge retain only the old field and lack the new one, meaning imports of those rows lose the template data. This same pattern seems relevant to ENG-2351 regarding older Roam rows as well.

I should send a heads-up to the ENG-2351 implementer, since SendMessage queues even to a running agent. For the sid decision, I'm weighing a producer-side backfill ticket (like schemaFormatBackfill) against a transitional consumer-side fallback in the Roam importer — leaning toward the backfill approach since existing heal paths (like regenerating embeddings) already rewrite every row, and a producer fix would automatically heal graphs synced before 2026-09-29 at their next sync, which matters since validation graphs likely predate that cutoff.

For #1505, my plan is to add the Risk line with the workaround noted (re-sync via embedding regeneration or editing the type page), note in a runbook that live testing requires the source graph's schema rows be rewritten after ENG-2202, then fix the citation in annotation 1 from #1267 to #1470, extend annotation 3 with the behavior-change sentence, and consider noting that `templateToText` drops something relevant.

I'm checking whether `nodeTemplateContent`, which replaced `templateToText` after ENG-2202, also drops Roam block headings at publish — the reviewer flagged this as optional, so I'll skip it. For the follow-up tickets, I'll ask sid whether he wants to file them or have me draft them using the engineering ticket tool with proper labeling, and then #1505 should be complete pending sid's decisions, the Loom video, and the live check — these are just PR metadata edits so no further code re-review should be needed.

For #1506, round 3 pushed a one-line fix, and rather than doing the closure check myself, I'll have the reviewer verify it quickly since it's cheap and keeps the workflow faithful, then I still need to send a heads-up to the ENG-2351 implementer.

I'll send three messages in parallel: to the ENG-2350 implementer with the body line fix and annotation edits, to the reviewer for closure confirmation on ac09d768, and to the ENG-2351 implementer flagging the legacy Roam rows issue where `template` holds the body but `template_content` is missing.

Confirmed: Roam switched from writing `literal_content.template` to `literal_content.template_content` after ENG-2202, so older unsynced rows lack a template — an issue affecting both ENG-2350 and the still-running ENG-2351. I'll send messages to the ENG-2350 implementer (PR note plus annotation fixes), the ENG-2348 reviewer (closure check), and the ENG-2351 implementer (heads-up on older rows).

16:  - Known limitation: the block-props copy that `createDiscourseNodeType` writes drops headings (`getBasicTreeByParentUid` carries no heading), so in the new settings store the Template tab and node creation show Obsidian `##` headings as plain blocks. Follow-up ticket to be filed.

19:  - Roam schemas synced before ENG-2202 shipped (2026-09-29) keep the template body in `literal_content.template` and have no `template_content` until a later sync rewrites them. ENG-2202 left that backfill out of scope, so importing those types brings no template. Any sync that rewrites the row fixes it (for example Generate & upload all node embeddings). Follow-up ticket to be filed for a producer-side backfill.

  PR #1508, head 42e6c4df (matches worktree HEAD; base origin/main 065cab5e is the merge base; `gh pr diff` is identical to `git diff origin/main...HEAD`). pre-pr-review mode: **Full**, because this is the first pass. The PR has no prior annotations, review threads, or reviews, and no last-reviewed SHA was given.
  
  ## 2. Findings (ranked)
  
  **P1: none.** I found no wrong behavior and no data loss. Every claim (a) to (e) checks out (details under "Open questions" below).
  
  **P2-1. `apps/roam/src/utils/exportUtils.ts:63-80` (`getContentFromNodes`): a third builder + extractor is still in Roam.**
  - How it differs from the shared one:
    - It builds its own regex, escaping `[ ] \ ^ $ . | ? * + ( )` but not braces.
    - It treats any `{[^}]+}` as a placeholder.
    - It matches `{content}` case-sensitively and doesn't trim.
    - It falls back to the title on an empty capture (`|| title`).
  - Why it matters: Done When 2 asks for one shared, unit-tested builder + extractor. The PR body says every matcher reads titles "through one builder and one extractor". Neither mentions this copy (Step 1a reuse gate, Step 4 deferral rule).
  - Fix: defer it with a ticket named under Risk or follow-up.
    - Don't swap it in this PR. It drives export file names, and the shared extractor would change them for formats without metacharacters (`{Content}` formats, padded titles), which Done When 3 rules out.
    - When it is swapped later, keep `|| title`. Otherwise an empty capture produces a `.md` file name.
  - Put the fill-side grammars in the same ticket. This mismatch predates the PR and is unchanged by it:
    - `formatUtils.ts:77,125` and `ModifyNodeDialog.tsx:398,492` fill `{[\w\d-]*}` tokens.
    - `Export.tsx:381` and `Tldraw.tsx:819` scan `{[\w\d-]+}`.
    - So node creation fills `{x1}`-style tokens that the shared builder matches as literal text.
  
  **P2-2. Stale Roam specifications (`DiscourseNodeSpecification.tsx:91,110`, read by `matchDiscourseNode.ts:22-32` and `discourseNodeFormatToDatalog.ts:13-16`): Done When 1 is still unmet for node types whose specification was generated before this PR.**
  - The specification stores the builder's regex once, when it is enabled.
  - The spec-based paths read that stored regex, not the format: `matchDiscourseNode`, and through it `findDiscourseNode`, the query builder and discourse context.
  - For `Claim (draft) - {content}` the stored regex never matches real titles. The format-based paths (sync, node search, `core_title`, `sourceIdOfNode`) now do match.
  - It isn't a regression, since the stored regex never matched before either. It's also graph-local: only `format` syncs (`conceptConversion.ts:74`).
  - The PR names the risk but gives no ticket and no user action.
  - Fix:
    - Ticket a value-aware rewrite: replace a stored target only when it equals the old builder's output for that format. Name the ticket in the PR.
    - State the workaround: turning the specification off deletes the scratch clause and turning it on regenerates it (`DiscourseNodeSpecification.tsx:56-72,126-139`).
  
  **P3-1. `apps/roam/src/utils/sourceSlot.ts:94-101`: the `{source}` lookup duplicates the placeholder-index-to-capture logic that `extractContentFromTitle.ts:11-16` now owns.**
  - Before this PR, both went through one `extractFieldFromTitle`.
  - The PR's reason for keeping it local ("the source slot hack is temporary") cites no retiring ticket.
  - The rewritten lookup is only tested with `{Source}` as the second placeholder (`sourceSlot.test.ts:85`).
  - Fix: either cite the retiring ticket (annotation A3), or export a generic `(format, title, placeholder) => string | undefined` from the package and build `extractContentFromTitle` on it. Also add a `{Source}: {content}` case.
  
  **P3-2. `packages/database/src/lib/__tests__/getDiscourseNodeFormatExpression.test.ts:8-16,31-41,56-62`: no test pins the brace escapes.**
  - JS treats a lone `{` or `}` as a literal, so the `{`/`}` per-character rows and the `{x1}` test still pass with braces dropped from the escape set. I checked this.
  - The JVM does not: an unescaped literal brace throws `Illegal repetition` (see A1).
  - Fix: add `["{x1} - {content}", "^\\{x1\\} - (.*?)$"]` to the source table.
  
  **P3-3. PR body precision.**
  - Parity row 3 says the Obsidian fallback change reaches bulk-identify patterns. `BulkImportCandidate.extractedContent` is written at `QueryEngine.ts:396,771` and read nowhere. So the only observable Obsidian change is the published `core_title` and the Content line, for imported node types without `{content}`.
  - Parity row 5 omits that `sourceIdOfNode` now uses the cached `matcherFor` regex instead of compiling one per call.
  - The guard removals aren't argued (Step 4). Annotations A3 and A4 cover them:
    - sourceSlot's `?.` before `.trim()`
    - `extractFieldFromTitle`'s `!node.format` and `length <= 1` checks
    - Obsidian's `if (!format) return title`
    - the view's `if (!format) return ""`
  
  ### Open questions (judged)
  - **Whole-title fallback: keep.** It matches Roam's extractor, `decorateTitle` returning null for the same formats (so decorate/undecorate stays consistent), and the ENG-2153 contract's fallback to the title. In Obsidian it's reachable only through imported node types: `validateNodeType.ts:31` refuses a format without `{content}` on save, and ENG-2323 confirms only `{content}` is supported. The decision isn't recorded anywhere (see Scope check).
  - **`formatUtils.ts` does not violate Done When 2.** It fills placeholders when creating a node. It is neither the regex builder nor the extractor, and Done When 2's minimum is that scan and builder share one grammar constant. `exportUtils.getContentFromNodes` is an extractor, so P2-1 applies to it.
  - **Old specifications:** no migration in this PR is acceptable, but it needs a ticket and the workaround (P2-2).
  - **Done When 2's view clause is adequately evidenced.** The view and the converter call the same function with inputs resolved the same way. `getNodeTypeById` and `nodeTypesById` both index `plugin.settings.nodeTypes` by the frontmatter `nodeTypeId` (`getDiscourseNodes.ts:34`), and both pass `file.basename`. The only display difference is that the view hides the line for an empty format. A render test would only re-test React interpolation. The Loom should show the Content line next to the published `core_title`.
  - **Claims verified:**
    - (a) Holds, with the P3-3 precision fix.
    - (b) Only titles that literally contain a `{x1}`-style token change.
    - (c) Braces are now escaped in stored-spec and datalog sources. This is harmless in JS and fixes a JVM failure.
    - (d) All 7 extractor call sites use `(format, title)`. All 3 reordered Roam sites have existing `coreTitle` tests that fail on a swap.

* Map major code, data, and UX surface that reads, writes, or infers `{Source}`.
* Evaluate the target relation model, naming, creation UX, and compatibility requirements for existing graphs.
* Propose migration and rollout options, including backfill, title normalization, collisions, ambiguous data, and idempotency.

* We have a recommended approach with affected surfaces, technical risks, test strategy, and rough implementation complexity.
* The proposal explains how new, existing, and customized graphs would behave during and after migration.

content.text:
Seven things. Item 1 is the only one holding up work right now; everything else already has a default applied or can wait until the PRs are ready.

**Blocking**
1. **ENG-2195 (#1507), Done When 2.** The rule "the result passes the existing format validation" is currently met only for invalid characters. As written, an imported format can end up identical to a local type's format. Obsidian would then refuse every save of the user's own local type, and this PR would be what introduced that.
   - **B (recommended):** if the normalized format still fails validation, fall back to the default built from the type name, and canonicalize `{Content}` to `{content}`. About 20–30 lines.
   - **A:** keep the character fix only and document the collision.
   - Separately, `specImport.ts` (importing schema files): defer it to a ticket (recommended), or include it now (about 4 lines).

**Decisions where I applied a default (say if you disagree)**

2. **ENG-2176 (#1508), whole-title fallback.** A format with no `{content}` now returns the whole title in both apps. I recommend keeping it. Once you confirm, I'll post a top-level "Decision:" comment on the PR.
3. **ENG-2350 (#1505) and ENG-2351 (#1510), older Roam rows.** Schema rows synced before ENG-2202 (Sep 29) hold the template in an old field, so both PRs import those types without a template.
   - My default is one producer-side backfill ticket rather than a fallback in each importer.
   - One question only you can answer: was the Sep 28 failure in ENG-2351 one of those old rows? If so, #1510 alone doesn't fix the reported case.

**Approvals for outward actions**

4. **Michael's "possible duplicate" comments on ENG-2195 and ENG-2176.** Can I post the drafted reply on both? It says the two aren't duplicates and overlap only on `^` and `|`. His assignee question on ENG-2195 is still yours to answer.
5. **Follow-up tickets.** Do you want to file these yourself, or should I draft them in Ticket Draft with `dg-create-engineering-ticket`?
   - Backfill `template_content` on older Roam schema rows. One ticket covers both #1505 and #1510.
   - Headings are dropped when an imported template is copied into the newer settings storage.
   - A failed markdown import can leave a half-created node type.
   - Roam's template export breaks multi-line blocks.
   - Roam's export has its own builder and extractor, plus the other placeholder scans.
   - Rewrite Roam specifications saved with the old regex.
   - Obsidian's template import panel skips Roam templates because they have no title.
   - Relation import matches built-in types like Page by label. This predates these PRs.
   - Optional: warn when a graph still has pattern relations that haven't been migrated.
6. **Push-pull Agent log.** Do you want milestone entries in Roam via propose_write? I'd need the UID of the Agent log block.

**Yours after this session**

7. **Loom and live check for each PR.** Every PR has a runbook. Videos happen in a separate session, as you've set it up. After that, mark each PR ready and assign reviewers. Your draft #1412 will need an import fix when you rebase it after #1508.

Smaller defaults already in the PRs, which you can override:
- **ENG-2348:** the warning links to the docs page rather than opening the settings dialog.
- **ENG-2351:** fallback template files are named `<type> (from <space>)`.
- **ENG-2349:** the 8px heading offset stays as it is.

content.text:
## ENG-2195 (#1507): the one decision blocking work

**What the PR does.** When Obsidian imports a Roam node and has no matching node type, it creates one using Roam's format, `[[CLM]] - {content}`. Brackets aren't allowed in Obsidian file names, which is how files like `[[CLM]] - sleep improves memory.md` happen. The PR strips the bad characters, so the format becomes `CLM - {content}`. That part works.

**The problem it creates.** Obsidian doesn't let two node types share a format. It checks this every time you save a node type in settings.

Example:
1. Your vault has a type called "Claims" with format `CLM - {content}`.
2. You import from Roam a type called "Claim" with format `[[CLM]] - {content}`.
3. The names differ, so the importer creates a new type. After stripping, its format is also `CLM - {content}`.
4. Now your own "Claims" type fails the duplicate check on every save, so you can't change anything on it, even its color. The imported type is read-only, so you can't fix it from that side either. The only way out is to rename your own type's format by hand.

Before this PR that collision couldn't happen, because nothing local ever had brackets. It only hits when the type names differ but the formats match. That's plausible, because Roam's default `[[CLM]]` and `[[QUE]]` strip down to exactly Obsidian's defaults.

**Your choice**
- **A. Ship as is.** Strip the characters only, and write the collision risk into the PR. It's simplest, and matches a narrow reading of the ticket. Michael, who wrote the ticket, judges it in review.
- **B. Add a fallback.** If the stripped format would collide, or is missing `{content}`, use the format the importer already falls back to when a schema has no format: the type name's first three letters. So "Claim" becomes `CLA - {content}`, and files come out as `CLA - sleep improves memory.md`, which no longer clashes with your `CLM` type. It's about 20–30 lines plus tests. ## How the Obsidian import works today

**Does the user get a choice?** Partly. In "Import nodes from another space" you pick the nodes, then an "Import preview" step lists the new node types it will create, by name only, e.g. "Claim" (`ImportNodesModal.tsx:453`). You can confirm or back out. You can't map an incoming type onto one of yours, and the preview never shows formats. Once you confirm, any new type is created automatically.

**Compare first, or import first?** Compare first, but only on id and name. Before creating anything, `findLocalNodeTypeMatch` looks for a local type with the same id, then the same name (case-insensitive). If it finds one, it reuses that type and never looks at the format. Only when nothing matches does it create a new type. Only then does it read the format, which this PR now strips. So the stripped format is never compared against your local formats, and that gap is where the duplicate comes from.

## Your idea: strip first, also compare formats, then import

In the example, the incoming "Claim" with `[[CLM]] - {content}` strips to `CLM - {content}`. Your "Claims" already has `CLM - {content}`, so the imported nodes go into "Claims" and no new type is created. There's no lockout, and no odd `CLA` prefix.

I didn't propose this because I treated id-then-name matching as fixed and only asked what to do after matching failed. That was too narrow. It's a real option, and I think it's the best one. Obsidian already forbids two types sharing a format, so an incoming type whose stripped format equals one of yours can't sit beside it anyway. It either joins your type (your idea) or takes a different format (my B).

What it costs:
- **It's a new matching rule.** Two types with different names get joined because their formats match. The project's Non-Goals exclude "automatic merging of incompatible local schemas". A matching format is strong evidence they're the same type, but Michael may still see this as more than ENG-2195 asked for, so the PR should say it plainly.
- **The preview has to change too.** It copies the id/name logic, so without the change it would show "Claim" as a new type while the import actually puts the nodes into "Claims". Ideally it shows "Claim → Claims (same format)".
- **Roam and Obsidian would match differently.** Roam's importer still matches by id and name only.
- **Size:** about 30 lines across the importer and the preview, plus tests. The `{Content}` → `{content}` fix is still needed separately.

**Updated options for #1507:**
- **C (your idea, my recommendation now):** match on the stripped format before creating, show the mapping in the preview, and fix the `{content}` case.
- **B:** create the new type with a renamed `CLA` prefix.
- **A:** ship as is and document the lockout.

Say C and I'll send it to the implementer.

content.text:
## What #1507 (ENG-2195) is about

**The bug:** you import a Roam node into Obsidian, and Obsidian doesn't have that node type yet. It copies Roam's format, `[[CLM]] - {content}`, so the file comes out as `[[CLM]] - sleep improves memory.md`. Brackets don't belong in Obsidian file names.

**The fix:** before saving the new type, the importer strips `# ^ [ ] |` from the format, so `[[CLM]] - {content}` becomes `CLM - {content}` and the file is `CLM - sleep improves memory.md`. It's 19 lines: one helper and one call.

## Is the duplicate-format problem new?

No. The importer on `main` never checks an incoming format against yours. This could already happen before the PR:
- **Obsidian to Obsidian:** another vault's "Claims" type uses `CLM - {content}` and yours is "Claim". The names differ, so a new type is created with the same format.
- **A schema with no format:** the importer makes one from the name. "Questions" gives `QUE - {content}`, which is Obsidian's default Question format.

What the PR adds is one more way in. Roam's defaults `[[CLM]]` and `[[QUE]]` strip to exactly Obsidian's defaults, so Roam imports now hit the old gap more often.

## Scope check against ENG-2195's Done When

1. **A type from `[[CLM]] - {content}` stores `CLM - {content}` and the file is `CLM - sleep improves memory.md`.** Met.
2. **Formats with `# ^ [ ] |` can't be saved un-normalized, and the result passes the existing format validation.** The first half is met. The second half is met for the character rules, which is what the Solution names ("apply the same invalid filename character checks"). The duplicate rule was never applied at import, before or after this PR.
3. **Tests cover brackets, other invalid characters, and valid formats left unchanged.** Met.

How each option lands:
- **A (the PR as it is):** inside scope. The duplicate gap goes to its own ticket and gets one line in the PR's Risk section.
- **B (rename to `CLA` on a collision):** a fix for an older problem, slipped into a bug-fix PR. Borderline.
- **C (match on format):** changes which type your nodes go into. No Done When item asks for that, the Solution says to leave existing matching unchanged, and it touches the project's Non-Goal on automatically merging schemas. Out of scope; it needs its own ticket and decision.

**So the scope check says A plus a ticket for "imports never check format uniqueness".** That reverses my earlier B recommendation. I had treated the collision as caused by this PR, and it isn't. The ticket can choose between B and C properly, for all three ways in, not just Roam's.

If you say go, the implementer will:
- add the Risk line;
- fix the PR body's wrong reason for skipping `specImport.ts`, and leave it out of this PR;
- apply the review's small fixes: normalize the name-derived default, reword a comment, fix one test title.

The duplication reply to Michael still waits on your OK.

**This also changes the older-rows question in your list.** The last Roam release (0.22.0, 2026-08-24) doesn't include ENG-2202. So every graph on the released extension still writes templates the old way, including probably the Sep 28 one. The first sync after the next Roam release rewrites those rows into the new shape. That makes the backfill ticket mostly unnecessary; only rows written by builds from `main` between Sep 1 and Sep 28 stay old. I've sent the corrected wording to #1505 and #1510.

I answered your question by running `scope-check` on the A/B/C fork. It settled two things: C is out of scope, and the duplicate-format problem is an older gap that needs its own ticket.

---
name: dg-create-engineering-ticket
description: Create concise Discourse Graphs Engineering tickets in Linear with the canonical template, correct readiness status, an active existing project, and existing labels. Use when the user asks to create or draft an Engineering ticket; do not use for Feedback tickets.
---

# DG Create Engineering Ticket

Create an Engineering ticket that another engineer can understand and implement without rediscovering its intent or scope.

Use `$dg-engineering-writing-style` when available. It is in the repository's `./.agents/skills` folder.

## Canonical template

The canonical Linear template is [General Engineering Task](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/new?template=6ca39698-3bce-449a-992e-059f0334e15b). Keep this link only as a reference in this skill. Never add it to a created ticket.

Use this exact template as the drafting checklist:

```markdown
## Problem

- What accepted user, developer, or project need does this address?
- Why does it need to be solved now?

## Solution

- What is the smallest change that solves the problem?

## Done When

- Describe how success is verified (behavioral or technical).
- Remember: Make only the smallest change needed to solve the problem.
- Remember: **Stay within the defined scope, or communicate any scope increase**

## Out of Scope

- (Optional) What adjacent cases, abstractions, or future work are explicitly not included?
- Link follow-up tickets where applicable

## Notes

- Additional Context, Blockers, dependencies, or follow-up actions.
```

Every bullet above is placeholder guidance. Replace or remove every placeholder before presenting a draft or creating a ticket. Keep all five headings, leaving `Out of Scope` or `Notes` empty when nothing useful applies. Use 1–3 short bullets per section unless the ticket is genuinely complex.

## Agent provenance and human review

Always use the Engineering team. This skill never creates or redirects to Feedback.

- Create every agent-created ticket in the existing `Ticket Draft` status with exactly one existing workspace provenance label from the `Created by` group. The label records provenance and stays after approval.
- Select the label from the creating agent's known identity: `Created by Claude` for Claude, `Created by Codex` for Codex, or `Created by LLM` for any other agent or when its identity cannot be determined. Do not infer agent identity from the Linear account, ticket topic, or skill name. Do not use `Created by LLM` as a substitute when the correct agent-specific label is missing.
- `Ticket Draft` is in the Backlog category and means human ticket review is pending; it does not authorize implementation. The existing `Draft` status belongs to the Started category and is used by the PR workflow. Do not use it for ticket review or change its automation.
- In `Notes`, record `Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket` and any other creation skills actually used. Skill attribution is provenance, not evidence that the ticket meets the standards.
- The human who asked the agent to create the ticket checks intent against the source request, scope and exclusions, verifiable acceptance criteria, and the canonical template and engineering writing standards. Keep the ticket in `Ticket Draft` while changes are needed.
- Human approval moves the ticket to `Backlog` when the problem and fix are agreed and implementation needs no further product or solution decisions. Use `Triage` when implementation is likely within six months but decisions remain. Keep idea-stage Engineering requests in Engineering.
- The human's move from `Ticket Draft` to `Triage` or `Backlog` records sign-off. An agent may make that move only after explicit human approval of the completed ticket and destination. A request to create a ticket is not approval of its generated contents. Keep the provenance label and skill attribution.

## Project selection

Every ticket must use an existing project that is not completed, canceled, archived, or trashed. Resolve the project in this order:

1. Use the project explicitly named by the user.
2. Use a clearly relevant active project from the current work context.
3. For Roam work, use `Roam Discourse Graph plugin assorted tasks`.
4. For Obsidian work, use `Obsidian Discourse Graphs plugin assorted tasks`.
5. Otherwise, use `Engineering Ops assorted tasks`.

Confirm the selected project still exists, is active, and includes the Engineering team. Never create a project. If a user-specified project is missing, ambiguous, or inactive, ask the user for another project instead of silently substituting one.

## Labels and optional fields

- Inspect existing issue labels and apply every clearly relevant label.
- Never create a label or guess an uncertain label.
- Missing or uncertain optional labels do not block creation. If `Ticket Draft` or the required provenance label is missing or ambiguous, return the prepared draft and report the configuration gap instead of creating an unmarked ticket or substituting a status.
- Set priority only when the user or context makes it clear and useful.
- Do not set a cycle or release. CI/CD handles releases.

## Create or draft

Draft without changing Linear when the user asks for a draft, review, or rewrite. Create the ticket without an additional confirmation when the user explicitly asks to create it.

Before creation, resolve the current Engineering statuses, selected project, and existing labels. Create the issue once with its title, completed description (including skill attribution), `Ticket Draft` status, project, provenance and relevant labels, and justified priority. If the result is ambiguous, search for the issue before retrying so a transient failure does not create a duplicate.

Read the created issue back and verify its status, labels, and attribution. Report any mismatch instead of claiming successful routing. Return the issue identifier, title, status, project, and link, and say that human review is pending. Include the generated branch name when Linear returns one. Do not restate the full description unless the user asks.

=================== WRITING STYLE
---
name: dg-engineering-writing-style
description: Draft and revise engineering emails, chat messages, requests, follow-ups, status updates, engineering tickets, PR comments, issue reports, release notes, technical documentation, and other team writing in the shared Discourse Graphs style. Use whenever a Discourse Graphs engineer asks to write, rewrite, phrase, shorten, clarify, or polish team communication or documentation, unless they request a different style.
---

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.
- Avoid em dashes as sentence-level punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses to separate thoughts instead. Preserve em dashes only when they appear in exact quotations, titles, source text, or technical content supplied by the requester.
- When identifying a problem or disagreement, state it plainly and pivot toward clarification, resolution, criteria, or next steps.
- Prefer bullets for distinct points. When prose reads more naturally, keep paragraphs and sentences short; avoid run-on sentences.
- Ask one clear question when one will do. Combine related questions only when separating them would add needless length.

## Adapt to the channel

- For a quick reply or chat message, omit the greeting and sign-off when they add no value.
- For technical issues, describe the observed behavior, the relevant contrast or expectation, and the requested clarification or next step.
- For engineering tickets and technical documentation, apply these ASD-STE100-inspired principles:
  - Use one term consistently for each concept. Do not alternate between synonyms.
  - Put one primary action or idea in each sentence.
  - Prefer active voice when the actor is important.
  - Replace vague verbs such as "handle," "support," or "improve" with the specific behavior or result.

## Drafting rules

- Preserve facts, commitments, dates, names, links, and technical meaning supplied by the requester.
- Do not invent availability, decisions, commitments, or emotional language.
- Treat explicit directions such as "shorter," "warmer," "more forceful," "broader," or "one sentence" as overrides for the current draft.
- When the requester asks for alternatives, vary the framing or emphasis rather than making superficial synonym swaps.
- Return a ready-to-use draft first. Add explanation only when requested or when an ambiguity materially affects the wording.
agents

input.title: Prevent imported Obsidian node types from duplicating a local node type's format
input.description:
## Problem

* When an import creates a node type, Obsidian stores the incoming format without checking it against local node types. A local node type with a different name can already use the same format.
* Obsidian then rejects every save of that local node type ("Format must be unique across all node types"). The imported node type is read-only, so the user must change the local format by hand.
* This already happens for formats from other Obsidian vaults and for name-derived default formats. ENG-2195 makes it more common, because Roam's default formats such as `[[CLM]] - {content}` normalize to Obsidian's default formats.

## Solution

* Before an import creates a node type, compare its normalized format with the formats of local node types.
* On a match, either map the incoming node type to the matching local node type or create it with a different format. This choice is open; see Notes.

## Done When

* Importing a node whose new node type's format matches a local node type's format leaves every local node type editable in settings.
* The import preview shows what the import does with that node type.
* Unit tests cover a matching format from a Roam schema, an Obsidian schema, and a name-derived default format.

## Out of Scope

* Node types that earlier imports already created with a duplicate format.
* Node type matching in Roam's importer.

## Notes

* Found in the ENG-2195 review (PR #1507). ENG-2195 stays limited to removing invalid characters.
* Open decision: mapping to the matching local node type adds format as a third matching rule after id and name, and changes which node type imported nodes join. The project's Non-Goals exclude automatic merging of local schemas. A different format keeps the node types apart but changes the imported node type's title prefix, for example `CLA - {content}` instead of `CLM - {content}`.
* Schema file import (`specImport.ts`) stores imported formats the same way. Decide whether it belongs here or in its own ticket.
* Relevant paths: `mapNodeTypeIdToLocal` and `parseSchemaLiteralContent` in `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts`, `findLocalNodeTypeMatch` in `apps/obsidian/src/utils/schemaMatching.ts`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importPreview.ts`, and `validateNodeFormat` in `apps/obsidian/src/utils/validateNodeType.ts`.
* Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket, dg-engineering-writing-style.

# DG Create Engineering Ticket

Create an Engineering ticket that another engineer can understand and implement without rediscovering its intent or scope.

Use `$dg-engineering-writing-style` when available. It is in the repository's `./.agents/skills` folder.

## Canonical template

The canonical Linear template is [General Engineering Task](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/new?template=6ca39698-3bce-449a-992e-059f0334e15b). Keep this link only as a reference in this skill. Never add it to a created ticket.

Use this exact template as the drafting checklist:

```markdown
## Problem

- What accepted user, developer, or project need does this address?
- Why does it need to be solved now?

## Solution

- What is the smallest change that solves the problem?

## Done When

- Describe how success is verified (behavioral or technical).
- Remember: Make only the smallest change needed to solve the problem.
- Remember: **Stay within the defined scope, or communicate any scope increase**

## Out of Scope

- (Optional) What adjacent cases, abstractions, or future work are explicitly not included?
- Link follow-up tickets where applicable

## Notes

- Additional Context, Blockers, dependencies, or follow-up actions.
```

Every bullet above is placeholder guidance. Replace or remove every placeholder before presenting a draft or creating a ticket. Keep all five headings, leaving `Out of Scope` or `Notes` empty when nothing useful applies. Use 1–3 short bullets per section unless the ticket is genuinely complex.

## Ticket readiness

Always use the Engineering team. This skill never creates or redirects to Feedback.

- Use `Backlog` when the problem is known, the fix is agreed upon, and another engineer can implement it without further product or solution decisions.
- Use `Triage` when implementation is likely within six months but the decision, scope, or solution is not fully settled.
- Keep an explicit Engineering ticket request in Engineering even when it is idea-stage.

## Project selection

Every ticket must use an existing project that is not completed, canceled, archived, or trashed. Resolve the project in this order:

1. Use the project explicitly named by the user.
2. Use a clearly relevant active project from the current work context.
3. For Roam work, use `Roam Discourse Graph plugin assorted tasks`.
4. For Obsidian work, use `Obsidian Discourse Graphs plugin assorted tasks`.
5. Otherwise, use `Engineering Ops assorted tasks`.

Confirm the selected project still exists, is active, and includes the Engineering team. Never create a project. If a user-specified project is missing, ambiguous, or inactive, ask the user for another project instead of silently substituting one.

## Labels and optional fields

- Inspect existing issue labels and apply every clearly relevant label.
- Never create a label or guess an uncertain label.
- Missing or uncertain labels do not block creation. After creation, tell the user when no label was applied or when label selection remained uncertain.
- Set priority only when the user or context makes it clear and useful.
- Do not set a cycle or release. CI/CD handles releases.

## Create or draft

Draft without changing Linear when the user asks for a draft, review, or rewrite. Create the ticket without an additional confirmation when the user explicitly asks to create it.

Before creation, resolve the current Engineering statuses, selected project, and existing labels. Create the issue once with its title, completed description, status, project, labels, and justified priority. If the result is ambiguous, search for the issue before retrying so a transient failure does not create a duplicate.

After creation, return the issue identifier, title, status, project, and link. Include the generated branch name when Linear returns one. Do not restate the full description unless the user asks.

input.description:
## Problem

* When an import creates a node type, Obsidian stores the format without checking it against local node types. A local node type with a different name can already use the same format.
* Obsidian then rejects every save of that local node type ("Format must be unique across all node types"). The imported node type is read-only, so the user must change the local format by hand.
* Formats from other Obsidian vaults and name-derived default formats can already cause this. ENG-2195 makes it more common, because Roam's default formats such as `[[CLM]] - {content}` normalize to Obsidian's default formats.

## Solution

* Before an import creates a node type, compare its normalized format with the formats of local node types.
* On a match, either map the imported node type to the matching local node type or create it with a different format. This choice is open; see Notes.

## Done When

* When an imported node type's format matches a local node type's format, the local node type still saves in settings after the import.
* The import preview shows what the import does with that node type.
* Unit tests cover a matching format from a Roam schema, an Obsidian schema, and a name-derived default format.

## Out of Scope

* Node types that earlier imports already created with a duplicate format.
* Node type matching in Roam's importer.

## Notes

* Follow-up to ENG-2195 (PR #1507), which stays limited to removing invalid characters. Schema file import (`specImport.ts`) stores formats the same way; decide whether this ticket covers it.
* Open decision: mapping adds format as a third matching rule after id and name, and changes which node type imported nodes join. The project's Non-Goals exclude automatic merging of local schemas. A different format keeps the node types apart but changes the imported title prefix, for example `CLA - {content}` instead of `CLM - {content}`.
* Relevant paths: `mapNodeTypeIdToLocal` in `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts`, `findLocalNodeTypeMatch` in `apps/obsidian/src/utils/schemaMatching.ts`, and `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importPreview.ts`.
* Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket, dg-engineering-writing-style.
